record.title: Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide — Artificial Intelligence Application Security Guidelines: General Provisions
record.original_title: 网络安全标准实践指南——人工智能应用安全指引 总则
record.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
record.summary: General part of TC260's AI application security guidelines, for all sectors, based on the Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection Laws and the rules on generative AI, AI content labelling, algorithmic recommendation and deep synthesis. It sets principles such as ultimate human control and graded protection, and guidance for each stage from planning to decommissioning: risk identification, five-level security grading, capability maturity assessment, one-click takeover, emergency shutdown, safety tests (also for minors), guardrails, content labelling, emergency plans and annual re-testing; it encourages unconditional relief for major personal-injury accidents.
record.notes: Version v1.0-202609, released on 15 Sept 2026 with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 together with sector guides for education, health, and radio, TV and network audiovisual services, to address new risks from the fast spread of AI applications. An organisation applying AI in a sector follows this guide and the sector document. The five security grades run from low to especially major security risk, and each party involved must reach a capability maturity level no lower than the application's grade; for grading and maturity assessment the guide refers to national standards on AI application security classification and grading and on AI security capability maturity. Normative references include GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), GB 45438-2025 (CN-08), GB/T 45674-2025, GB/T 45652-2025 and TC260-005, AI Application Ethics Security Guidelines 1.0. Because responsibility for AI failures is hard to assign, it encourages arrangements in applications involving personal safety for immediate, unconditional humanitarian relief after major personal-injury accidents.

verification.note: Stored from tc260.org.cn: the guide's PDF (version v1.0-202609) and the release notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 of 15 Sept 2026 with the four guides attached to it. Title, number, issuer, date and contents are confirmed from these; the summary follows the Chinese text. No English version was found.

judgment.status_reasoning: The TC260 Secretariat released the guide with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 of 15 Sept 2026 (关于发布 ... 的通知, a release notice, not a call for comments); the cover carries a released version number (v1.0-202609) and no draft marking (征求意见稿). The preface describes practice guides as technical documents the TC260 Secretariat drafts and publishes to give practical guidance, so it is not binding; no later version is stored. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.date_reasoning: The notice's posting date (发布时间) and signature date are both 15 Sept 2026.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific security guidance from TC260, the national cybersecurity standardisation committee, covering the full AI application life cycle: a government safety and risk-management guideline (AGENTS.md section 10, in with no note).
judgment.instrument_type_reasoning: TC260 practice guides are 'standard-related technical documents' giving practical guidance, not national standards; recorded as Guidelines / framework.
